races.name: Forte Healthcare Handicap

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: Has a 2-from-6 win-or-place record at 6f on Good going and maps as the race's sole pace-maker; 14 days fresh with DBM aboard, its STYLE_FIT flag suggests it is marginally racing outside its most comfortable role but it is still the one that controls the tempo.

runners_data.name: Ohailbhic
runners_data.note: Returns from 124 days off having last run on Standard ground at 7-8f trips — both the sharp step back in trip and the absence are significant queries, though John James Feane has just one placing from six runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Bad Boy Rizz
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a 3yo with a strong placed record at 5-6f on Good turf (7 from 9 sim-going runs), and the headgear entry alongside a 49-day break for Ross O'Sullivan who fires one winner from 15 recent starts; fits the prominent profile ideally for this shape.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type at 7 years old whose recent form reads 4th-5th-10th at longer trips on Soft/Standard, and the step to 6f Good looks optimistic; Adam Caffrey takes the ride for an in-form McGuinness yard (2 from 28 past fortnight).

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse rides a 3yo filly who won over 5f on Good and recorded a 6f Good run recently, making her the most trip-and-going-compatible prominent type after Bad Boy Rizz; 21 days between runs and Marnane has two winners from 20 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Four Blondes
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner with solid 6f Good course credentials (12 sim-going runs, placed twice); recent form includes a 4th over course and distance, and Donagh O'Connor keeps the ride for a Ross O'Sullivan yard that has produced one winner from 15 recently.

runners_data.name: Ninth Crusade
runners_data.note: Last run was 243 days ago and all recent form came on Standard ground at shorter trips, so both the layoff and the going/trip switch to Naas 6f Good create real uncertainty; Colin Keane's booking is the main positive.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Won over this course and trip on Good going and carries the highest sim-going score (9 from 15), but races from further back than its natural style suits — a true prominent type pushed into midfield by the congestion ahead, and the STYLE_FIT penalty is meaningful here.

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: Another horse whose natural front-running instincts are compromised by the crowded prominent berths; 45 days since last run and recent form of 10-8-4-8-7 at 5-6f on Good/Soft gives little encouragement even if it does find a clean passage from midfield.

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a 3yo flagged for fading in the finish, and its last five runs all came on Good ground at Naas/similar tracks — but it too is a genuine prominent type who will be unable to assert its style, having been pushed into midfield by traffic, and that finishing trend makes it risky.

runners_data.name: Unidos
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear; Gavin Ryan rides for the same Fahey yard as I Bid You Ajou, and its sim-going record of 3 from 5 on Good is modest — trainer's 14-day record of 0 from 7 adds little confidence.

races.paceDynamic: I Bid You Ajou is the lone confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop over this flat Naas 6f, with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead. The redistribution flags on Gotta Catch'em All, Mint Man, and All Hail are significant — all three are natural prominent types who will be unable to slot into their preferred position, meaning they will race wide or slightly further back than ideal, adding bodies in midfield rather than pressuring the pace. Bad Boy Rizz and Soulful Diva are the prominent types most likely to secure berths closest to I Bid You Ajou, given their style and freshness, while Ohailbhic has the profile but a very long absence. With a single front-runner setting a comfortable tempo unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce in the final furlong, rather than deep closers who need a pressured gallop to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If I Bid You Ajou controls from the front without pressure and the pace is fair-to-honest throughout.
scenarios.body: I Bid You Ajou sets a sustainable fractions and the two closest chasers, likely Bad Boy Rizz and Soulful Diva, are best placed to strike as the leader ties up; a horse that races prominently and relaxes well will pick the pieces cleanly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent stalkers settles beautifully two lengths off the pace and accelerates past a tying I Bid You Ajou in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: The generous pace from a single leader allows a well-placed prominent horse to save ground and produce a clean run; Bad Boy Rizz's sharp 5f-6f form on Good turf and prior placed runs make it the most natural beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and the leader burns out, creating a gap for hold-up horses to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Flaming Rib and Four Blondes are genuine hold-up types and would benefit from late gaps, though Naas 6f flat rarely produces a strong enough end-to-end pace to generate the kind of collapse needed for deep closers to dominate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Tactical Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners push forward early and the race turns chaotic with no clean run for any horse.
scenarios.body: A messy pace scenario with several prominent types crowding the early stages could produce a stop-start gallop that scrambles all expectations, though this is unlikely given the redistribution keeping most prominent types off the pace; Ninth Crusade and Unidos would be marginal gainers from a truly muddling pace.

watchPoints.text: I Bid You Ajou leads completely unchallenged — watch whether it gets a soft lead that allows it to conserve energy and hold on, rather than being reeled in by Bad Boy Rizz or Soulful Diva in the final furlong.
Gotta Catch'em All, Mint Man, and All Hail are all natural prominent types forced wide or into midfield — watch for early crowding on the far side as they jostle for position in the first furlong.
Ohailbhic's 124-day absence combined with a significant drop from 7-8f on Standard to 6f on Good means its fitness and trip suitability are genuine unknowns — watch for it to be outpaced early.

Ninth Crusade has not run in 243 days and Colin Keane's booking may attract support, but all form was on Standard ground — watch market moves as a guide to stable confidence rather than treating the form at face value.

All Hail and Unidos are both flagged for fading in the finish — if either appears prominent early, watch for them to drop away sharply from the 1f pole, which could create a late opening for Flaming Rib or Four Blondes.

races.name: Arqana Irish EBF Marwell Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: April Mist
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f Good at this course and placed over same trip — the Colin Keane booking for a Lyons yard in form is significant; sits naturally prominent and the course-and-distance form makes her a model fit for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Back To The Lodge
runners_data.note: Beaten favourite on sole start (11th, 6f Good) and flags a tendency to fade late — Ben Coen takes over but this horse is a hold-up type stepping into Listed company off just one run with a worrying form string.

runners_data.name: Belle Of The Ball
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Harrington runner who naturally wants to race prominently, but with so many pace-committed rivals she is unlikely to secure that position and will effectively race from a less comfortable slot — the 0/3 Going record in sim conditions adds a further small concern.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: Has won once and placed three times over 5f Good, showing genuine course aptitude, but this Twomey runner is a naturally prominent horse who will be crowded out early by stronger rivals; the headgear flag and the redistribution away from his preferred spot temper his claims despite the solid course figures.

runners_data.name: Concorde Landed
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in one start over 5f Good for P Twomey — same trainer as Big Negotiator — and WJ Lee takes over; wins on identical going and trip, and tracking Shesthedevil from a prominent pitch is exactly where he wants to be, making the form line worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Eastern Queen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (one run, fifth over 5f Good) with no real hold-up form to assess; the redistribution to rear reflects a field light on true closers rather than her own style, and Nathan Crosse's low-profile yard makes this a significant step up in class.

runners_data.name: Shesthedevil
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, won recently over 6f Good for Patrick Magee, and Chris Hayes takes over; she'll stride into the lead uncontested and the question is purely whether her speed is good enough to sustain it at Listed level over 5f.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: A Newmarket-trained Harry Eustace runner with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle — won over 5f Good on debut and this is a step up to Listed; wants to race prominently but this field has no room for another prominent horse, so she'll find herself further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Silent Beauty
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Soft for Belgian handler Kevin Philippart De Foy, placed at 6f Good on the other start — the drop to 5f Good is a query, though she is naturally prominent and if she handles the trip she's right in the pocket position to benefit from the scenario.

runners_data.name: Tropical Crown
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in one start over 5f Good for Karl Burke, ridden by Pierre-Louis Jamin — both trainer and jockey land here with strong recent form (T14: 7/36); naturally prominent, and if she gets a clean pitch off Shesthedevil's heels she has the profile of a horse that could quicken decisively.

races.paceDynamic: Shesthedevil is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no natural rival to press her, she should stride into an uncontested lead from the off and control the tempo over this straight 5f on Good ground at Naas. Behind her, a cluster of prominent-minded types — April Mist, Concorde Landed, Tropical Crown, and Silent Beauty — will jostle for the favoured positions in the first two furlongs, creating genuine traffic danger and potential shuffling between the 2f and 3f markers. Belle Of The Ball, Shimmering Sun, and Big Negotiator are all naturally prominent horses who cannot all secure their preferred position in this congested field and will be forced wider or further back than ideal, meaning their redistribution to midfield reflects circumstance rather than choice. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a sustainable gallop ahead of prominent-type congestion — strongly favours horses who can sit a length or two off the pace in a genuine prominent position and quicken when the leader is collared inside the final furlong, rather than true hold-up horses who will have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shesthedevil Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil bowls along uncontested and the prominent chasers pick her off inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Shesthedevil sets a controlled, honest gallop and the contest becomes a sustained dash home, with the best prominent horses — those who tracked without burning energy in the early jostle — having the decisive late kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrum Causes Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the early congestion behind Shesthedevil results in significant interference that shuffles the pack and opens the door for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: The bumping and checking between the prominent group at halfway creates a disorganised race shape where cleaner air and a wider, unimpeded run becomes the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Shesthedevil Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil's pace proves genuinely sustainable on this going and the chasers leave their runs fractionally too late.
scenarios.body: Rather than being caught, Shesthedevil extends past the furlong pole and the prominent group's energy burned in early positioning leaves them with insufficient finishing speed to reel her in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble for prominence is severe enough to slow the overall early fractions, gifting the hold-up runners a rare opening.
scenarios.body: Back To The Lodge or Eastern Queen would need the race to fall apart tactically in front of them, an unlikely outcome given Shesthedevil's lone front-running role creates a clean, fair-paced contest that rarely suits true hold-up types over 5f.

watchPoints.text: Watch the prominent pack — April Mist, Concorde Landed, Tropical Crown, and Silent Beauty all want the same tracking position behind Shesthedevil, and the first 2f of this 5f dash are likely to see sharp checks and bumping that could cost one or more of them valuable lengths.

Shesthedevil (Chris Hayes) is uncontested on the front end but steps sharply up in class to Listed; if she sets a slow enough gallop under a confident ride, the prominent group behind may be caught flat when she quickens — watch for an unexpected front-running performance.

Belle Of The Ball, Shimmering Sun, and Big Negotiator are all naturally prominent types forced into midfield by congestion — if any of them work hard to recover their preferred position in the first furlong, they may arrive at the business end with their petrol already spent.

Back To The Lodge is flagged as fading in the finish and returns from 38 days off into Listed company on her second career start — if the race develops into a slog any horse with stamina doubts over 5f will be found out late, and she is the most exposed candidate.

Tropical Crown (Burke/Jamin, T14: 7/36) arrives on the back of a dominant debut, with trainer and jockey both firing — the combination is worth monitoring for any pre-race confidence signals that might not yet be reflected in early market shows.

races.name: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Chantez
runners_data.note: Has struggled to recapture form that earned her earlier placed efforts, showing a 638-54 string that suggests she's been running below her OR=93 mark; prominent runner for Lyons/Keane but trips have been 7f-8f recently and dropping back to 6f asks a question, albeit on her optimal good ground.

runners_data.name: Fregada
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan takes over on a mare whose 0-9664 string looks grim on paper but includes two fourth-place finishes in competitive handicap company; genuine hold-up type who needs a true gallop to unlock her finishing effort, and the going is fine but recent form is unconvincing.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 5f who has finished second or placed in five of her last 10 starts, but has never won beyond 5f and now faces a stiffer 6f Listed test; Declan McDonogh keeps the ride and she holds up naturally, needing a pace collapse she may not get here.

runners_data.name: Little Queenie
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who landed a 6f win 45 days ago before a run of placed efforts; Robert Whearty-ridden hold-up type whose sim-going record is adequate but 1W3P from 15 good-ground runs tells you she places more than she wins, and this is competitive Listed grade.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's four-year-old is in the form of her life with two recent 5f wins including a soft-ground success, and JP Sheridan's booking is notable; her natural prominent style suits the race shape here, though the step up from 5f to 6f and into Listed company is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type by profile, placed into a midfield mapping because the rear is overcrowded — she won over 6f on good ground earlier in the year and Chris Hayes knows her well; the redistribution means she may not get the back-of-the-field position from which she operates best, which tempers her chance in a prominent-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's progressive mare has won two of her last four and is ideally suited racing up with the pace, but with so many prominent types in this field, Ben Coen will face a fight to secure her natural berth; her form figures of 3-2211 are strong, though the redistribution constraint means she could end up racing out of her rhythm if the early positions are taken.

runners_data.name: Soul Love
runners_data.note: Burke's three-year-old is the confirmed front-runner, carrying the highest OR in the field at 101, and Jamin should get a clean lead from a 15-runner field; two recent 6f wins and a good-ground record suggest she is capable of controlling the race, though the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that sustained pressure from a field this deep could expose her.

runners_data.name: Coconut Cove
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old won over 6f at Sandown last time out and Jack Mitchell knows how to deploy him from a prominent position; sim-going record is modest at 0W2P on good turf so the surface may not be a true concern but he is yet to prove himself at this level against mares.

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's rapidly improving three-year-old has won back-to-back over 6f-7f, ridden prominently throughout; his natural style is to race close to the pace but in a field this congested he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal — his two wins suggest he has a sharp turn of foot that could still be deployed if gaps appear.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Gavin Ryan's three-year-old ran just four days ago which is an aggressive turnaround for a 6f Listed race; naturally wants to be prominent but the redistribution means she is likely to be shuffled back, and her OR=76 is the lowest in the field, making the class jump a significant obstacle regardless of pace position.

runners_data.name: Oh Cecelia
runners_data.note: Shane Foley on a three-year-old whose visored OR=100 run yielded an unlucky ninth last time, but she has won over 5f on soft and placed over 6f on good ground; genuine hold-up type who needs a truly run race to unleash her finishing effort, and the controlled tempo Soul Love is likely to set is her biggest enemy.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: Joseph Murphy's three-year-old showed a 0-5235 string that includes solid placed efforts at 6f on good ground, and Gary Carroll is a smart tactical jockey; prominent style suits the expected race shape well, and if he can sit a length or two off Soul Love he is ideally positioned to pounce inside the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Xerling
runners_data.note: Lupini's three-year-old has a sharp sim-going record of 1W3P from 6 good-ground runs and won over 5f recently, stepping up to 6f here; Wayne Lordan is a strong rider for this type of prominent, pressing race, and the horse's profile is one of the better fits for the expected pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Yellowstone Lake
runners_data.note: Pat Twomey's three-year-old won over 7f on standard and has a prominent style, but hasn't run for 45 days which is the longest break in the field; WJ Lee takes the ride and the horse wants to race close to the pace, though the wider field and traffic will likely push him further back than his best form demands — the layoff is also an unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Soul Love is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead from stall, Pierre-Louis Jamin should be able to control the tempo on good ground over 6f at Naas — a sustainable, uncontested gallop that keeps the race honest without turning it into a burn-up. Behind her, a significant traffic jam of genuine prominent types exists: Treasure Rose, Dancing Saxon, Yellowstone Lake, Focaccia and others all want to race prominently but the map cannot accommodate them all, meaning several will be shuffled into a midfield position that does not suit their natural style — most likely to actually secure prominent spots are Tahcawin, Xerling and Coconut Cove given their stall positions and rider intent. The hold-up brigade — Oh Cecelia, Fregada, Little Queenie and Likedbymike — will have cover to hunt from but face the classic Naas 6f problem: a controlled pace rarely generates the sprint room that late closers need. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently just behind the leader and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep closers who need the pace to collapse in front of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soul Love Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Soul Love dictates an uncontested, metronomic gallop and the prominent stalkers time their challenge to peak in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Soul Love's ability to set her own fractions on good ground means the pace is genuine but not brutal, rewarding horses that travel in the first three and can sustain their effort; the compact nature of a 6f Listed contest under these conditions historically suits that mid-prominent profile over outright closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the scramble for prominent positions among the redistributed horses causes early friction and the pace becomes ragged, leaving fresh legs at the back.
scenarios.body: Oh Cecelia has shown she can finish powerfully from off the pace and, with Shane Foley likely to deploy her hold-up strengths, she is best placed to benefit if the field strings out unevenly; Fregada and Little Queenie also carry genuine finishing pace but need the tempo to be higher in the middle stages than this shape typically delivers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Fail, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Soul Love bowls along at a pace that the prominent stalkers cannot quicken past, and the closers are caught too far back.
scenarios.body: A genuinely dominant front-runner holding a clear lead at the two-furlong pole on good ground can win from the front at Naas, and Soul Love's OR=101 and 1-1 back-to-back wins here gives her the class ceiling to do it; this scenario discounts the redistributed prominent types who will be racing out of their natural rhythm.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the logjam of prominent types causes interference mid-race and opens a gap for a horse tracking just off the pace at a big price.
scenarios.body: Dancing Saxon's two consecutive wins suggest he has a sharp acceleration that could exploit chaos ahead of him, and Yellowstone Lake's natural tactical speed means either could thread through if the field bunches and splits late; both are shown redistributed from their true prominent role, so this scenario requires an untidy race and is accordingly lower probability.

watchPoints.text: Soul Love has the highest OR and a clear lead, but Pierre-Louis Jamin must judge the tempo carefully — if she is allowed to coast too slowly, the pursuing pack of prominent types will accelerate past her in the final furlong and she will be vulnerable despite her superior rating.

The scramble for prominent ground between Treasure Rose, Dancing Saxon, Yellowstone Lake, Tahcawin and Xerling in the early stages of a 15-runner 6f race is a significant interference risk — watch the first two furlongs carefully for crowding on the stands rail.

Oh Cecelia is equipped with a visor and Shane Foley has shown he will drop her in and wait for a gap; if the field fans wide at the two-furlong pole she could appear from an unexpected angle, making her a danger watch even if the pace scenario does not fully suit her.

Focaccia ran just four days ago and, while connections are clearly confident, the short turnaround for a three-year-old in Listed company is worth monitoring in the pre-race parade — any sign of a flat coat or dull eye should downgrade her chance significantly.

Yellowstone Lake's 45-day absence is the longest in the field; P Twomey runs horses fresh and this track-distance combination is feasible, but watch the betting market for any significant drift that would suggest connections are treating this as a fitness run rather than a winning mission.

races.name: O'Neill & Co. Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse at 8f on Good — this is the trip and ground she has placed at twice in recent form, but from OR 60 she carries top weight and Conor Cusack takes a 2lb claim; has never won on turf Good, finishing 7th last time out, and needs others to do the donkey work before she can challenge.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a warning flag for fading in the finish — the fade note is damaging in a race likely to be run at a fair clip only late; three runs back he finished 3rd at 9f on Good which represents his best recent effort, but the 7-day turnaround and pattern of finishing positions (8,7,3,?,7) give little confidence.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's hold-up type has been busy, running 7 days ago; his best recent effort was a 3rd at 9f on Good and he is drawn wider in an 18-runner field; headgear (tongue-tie and blinkers) keeps him switched on but his sim-going record of 0W2P over 14 turf runs on similar ground is unspectacular.

runners_data.name: Slaney Swagger
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has produced his best at 8f on Good (3rd last in that sphere), although his recent form shows two 10th-place finishes; the visor is retained and he is 13 days fresh — if there is any late pace collapse this is one of the more interesting profiles given his 8f Good placed form, but he needs things to go right.

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose form on Good ground at 8f shows an 11th last time out; OR 54 and blinkers fitted, but sim-going record of 6/15 on Good turf suggests the surface is not an issue — the concern is the flat staying form over 16f trips in his recent history, which raises doubts about whether a sharp 1m suits.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and the linchpin of this entire race shape; won at 8f on Good on his latest success and is well-suited by this course, distance and going combination (sim-going 12/15); an 8-year-old who is comfortable on the front end, carrying OR 53 with a 2lb claim, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) here is misleading — he IS in his natural role and is the horse most likely to control the race.

runners_data.name: Mehmar
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by inclination who has been mapped to midfield purely because the rear of the race is congested with similar types — his actual racing pattern is off the pace; six-day turnaround, OR 52, and his recent form over 5-6f trips raises an obvious distance concern at 1m; the STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) is warranted given the mismatch between natural position and where he will likely race.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Lohengrin's record of 10,10,11,14,20 over the last five runs on Good ground tells its own story — a genuine hold-up horse who has been placed to midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded, but his real racing style is well back; the fade warning compounds the problem, and 0W1P from 15 Good-ground starts is deeply modest.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type whose natural position is at the back of the field — the fade warning is relevant in a race where the front-runner is likely to be well-reserved; his 5th at 9f on Good three runs back shows some aptitude for the trip, but 0W0P over 15 Good-turf runs and a pattern of fading make him hard to support; mapped to midfield purely through overcrowding at the rear.

runners_data.name: Akashaa
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old hold-up horse who has placed twice at 8f on Tapeta and once at 9f on Good — the Good turf sim-going record (5/8) is more limited than most rivals; tongue-tie worn, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects that she is pushed forward from her natural rear position by field congestion rather than any change in racing pattern.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: One of only three genuine prominent-type runners in the field and therefore in a position of tactical advantage; has placed twice at 8f — once on Good (5th) and once on Tapeta (2nd) — and the trainer has sent out three winners from 8 runners in the last 14 days; Sadhbh Tormey's 2lb claim adds value.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a fade warning placed to midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; her form figures of 8,14,13,22,10 are deeply unencouraging and sim-going shows only 4 finishes of note from 7 on Good turf; 14 days since her last run, but nothing in the record to suggest a change in fortunes.

runners_data.name: Pick A Window
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old hold-up type who has raced primarily over 6-7f — stepping up to 1m is an untested trip and introduces a genuine stamina question; her fade warning compounds the mismatch, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) reflects that she is occupying a map position she would not naturally hold in a less-congested rear field.

runners_data.name: Quarry Stone
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has finished 21st, 12th, 13th, 8th and 14th over her last five runs — the 8th on Tapeta over 6f is her best effort but at 1m on Good this is an entirely different test; fade-flagged and STYLE_FIT adjusted; trainer has only one runner in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: A 275-day absence is the dominant flag here — Denise Foster sends her back after nearly nine months off and all her recent runs have been over 10-12f, making a drop to 1m and an absence combination a difficult ask; a hold-up horse mapped to midfield through congestion, OR 40, and no win from five 10f+ runs on Good.

runners_data.name: Lorr's Girl
runners_data.note: Has one win in her career (at 7f on Tapeta) and recent form shows two last-place finishes; a hold-up horse whose map position reflects overcrowding at the rear rather than any tactical shift — Jimmy Dalton claims 2lbs but the 42-day break and OR 40 place this well down the pecking order.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been placed once at 10f on Good and once at 8f; the tongue-tie and visor combination is retained, and his 13-day turnaround is straightforward; however, 0W1P from 15 Good-turf runs and a recent string of 3,8,7,5,7 finishes offers limited grounds for optimism, and he sits at the bottom of the weights at OR 40.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: One of only three prominent-type horses and therefore occupies a privileged tactical position in this shape; recent form includes a 3rd at 8f on Good and a 4th at 8f on Good/Yielding — the trip and going both suit; trainer has had a quiet 14 days (0/3) but Mullacash Buzz's ability to travel close to Dinamine gives her a straightforward race regardless of trainer form.

races.paceDynamic: Dinamine is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with Famous Enough and Mullacash Buzz as the only other prominent-style horses, the pace is thin at the front and almost certain to be sustainable rather than searingly fast. Dinamine sets off from stall 6 at Good ground over a flat mile at Naas — conditions that suit a horse who has already won over this course and distance — and with no rival likely to seriously push her for the lead, she can dictate a measured gallop that may never truly quicken the field. The bulk of the field are genuine hold-up horses, but the race is overloaded with them: Mehmar, Lohengrin, Morning Approach, Peig Sayers, Pick A Window and others have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are not enough front positions for all of them, and their actual pattern is to race well off the pace. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or in the first half of the field without being committed to the very front, because a controlled pace with a capable front-runner sets up a situation where the lead or near-lead position is never relinquished — deep closers from the rear are unlikely to generate enough momentum on Good ground over a flat mile to peg back a relaxed leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dinamine controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dinamine is allowed to bowl along at her own pace and Famous Enough / Mullacash Buzz settle in behind without pressuring her.
scenarios.body: Dinamine sets a measured, uncontested tempo, conserves energy through the middle sections, and kicks off the home turn to win going away; the flat Naas mile with no undulations removes any stamina risk and suits a front-runner who can dictate the fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate finish
scenarios.trigger: If Famous Enough or Mullacash Buzz track Dinamine closely and outfinish her in the closing furlong.
scenarios.body: A modestly-run race sees the first three or four finishers emerge from the front half of the field as the field strings out and hold-up horses can never close the gap; Famous Enough's placed form at 8f on Good and Mullacash Buzz's consistent proximity suit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield stalker swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally faster than expected and Dinamine ties up, allowing a horse tracking in fifth or sixth to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Slaney Swagger or Perfect Judgement, both capable of racing handily when settled, benefit if the pace-setter has done enough work to blunt the leader's finish; Perfect Judgement has placed form at 8f on Good and Slaney Swagger's recent 3rd at 8f on Good is a live pointer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True closer lands from rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and genuine hold-up horses can close from well back — a lower-probability shape given how many of the rear-runners are redistributed types.
scenarios.body: Mehmar or Akashaa would need the race to collapse entirely in front of them, but both carry STYLE_FIT warnings and are not operating in their most natural position in this shape; the Going is Good rather than soft, limiting the stamina-sapping conditions that would favour a late rattle.

watchPoints.text: Dinamine's ability to control the pace unchallenged is the single most important factor — watch whether Famous Enough or Mullacash Buzz attempt to match strides early, as any pressure on the front-runner transforms this race shape entirely.

With 18 runners in an apprentice handicap, the initial scramble for position could see several of the redistributed hold-up horses (Mehmar, Morning Approach, Lohengrin) pushed further forward than their natural style — watch for traffic congestion on the home turn as they attempt to find a run from midfield.

William F Browne and Lohengrin both carry fade warnings and have run within the last seven days — watch their energy levels in the closing furlong, as repeated quick returns on Good ground can blunt a horse's finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: Has posted consistent 2-3-3 placed efforts at 7f on Good ground and arrives just 26 days fresh; the sole confirmed pace-setter here means he controls the fractions, but Anthony McCann's stable is winless in 6 starts over 14 days and finishing off a run of placed efforts without winning may expose a ceiling.

runners_data.name: Barbapapa
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old owns a 1-6f win and three placed efforts in similar company, but his last two outings on Good ground were 9th and 12th — he is a true front-runner by instinct who will be crowded out for early position here, an unfamiliar constraint that the 38-day break may not resolve.

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Soft last time but the step back to Good and out to 7f is a different task; a genuine pace-seeker by nature, he faces the same positional squeeze as the other redistributed prominent types, and Feane's yard is cold over 14 days (0/6 T14).

runners_data.name: Watch Tower
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over for G M Lyons, whose yard is in good form (6/25 T14), and Watch Tower's last three starts all show a 7f/Good affinity including a win at this course — the natural prominent style needs no adjustment and he is the cleanest positional fit behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Blues Emperor
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse on paper but recent returns show 12th, 6th, 13th and 16th in his last four turf starts — the headgear (tp) has not sparked a revival and William Harvey's near-empty string (0/1 T14) limits confidence; only a genuinely strong pace over this 7f would give him any realistic closing chance.

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Comes back to 7f on Good having been placed twice at 7f-8f on similar ground, but his last five starts read 9-3-9-6-3 with the places coming on Soft; a true prominent type pushed into midfield by the crowded pace map, and Adrian McGuinness holds 2/28 over 14 days — modest angle.

runners_data.note: [Duplicate runner — covered above; entry retained for completeness. See above note.]

runners_data.name: Contrary To Law
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's three-year-old won over 7f Good most recently and is reunited with Ben Coen — the most compelling form line among the redistributed prominent group and the one most likely to push forward and secure a real position; hg:h (hood) may aid focus, and 14 days since last run is a routine turnaround for this yard.

races.paceDynamic: Little Empire is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should dictate an honest but uncontested gallop across Naas's flat seven furlongs. Watch Tower and Thenandnow are the only true prominent types who can legitimately travel close to the pace without redistribution; the rest of the stated prominent runners — Barbapapa, Spodo Komodo, Eddie G, and Contrary To Law — are genuine front-of-the-field horses who cannot all hold their natural position and will be forced to settle further back than ideal. With a single leader setting a controlled, even tempo on Good ground, the race shape is most likely to reward runners who can sit a length or two off the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp late burst — making the close-up prominent profile the primary beneficiary. The field holds materially more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate; of those redistributed, Contrary To Law (freshest, recent winner at 7f Good) and Barbapapa are most likely to press forward and secure a genuine prominent pitch if they choose to do so.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Close-Up Win
scenarios.trigger: If Little Empire dictates an uncontested, even pace and the race is decided by horses travelling prominently within two lengths of the leader.
scenarios.body: Little Empire bowls along at a sustainable clip, and the runners best-placed to exploit a calm tempo are those tracking directly behind who never use surplus energy; Watch Tower and Thenandnow, genuine prominent types with no redistribution penalty, are ideally suited to pounce from a close-up position in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grab Positions
scenarios.trigger: If Contrary To Law, Barbapapa, or another redistributed horse pushes up aggressively to challenge Little Empire, creating more genuine pace and a harder early gallop.
scenarios.body: A contested early tempo stretching the field out on Naas's flat track burns off those who over-committed, and the race becomes a test of stamina and grit in the final furlong; Contrary To Law, a recent 7f Good winner, is the most credible of the crowded prominent group to emerge from a true gallop having sat in a strong pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and leave Blues Emperor or a hold-up runner with daylight to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: Blues Emperor has the deepest closing profile in the race and benefits most if Little Empire's control paradoxically flatters the front while tiring the runners who chased too keenly; the issue is that Blues Emperor's recent form (80-40-60) and his tendency to race over 8f make a 7f Good-ground finish a stretch, though the fractions must genuinely accelerate to open up his lane.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Shape, Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to yield their position and create a scrappy, uneven tempo with surges and checks through the first half.
scenarios.body: A race with no rhythm and positional battles in the first three furlongs will see the field bunch and the pace fluctuate, making early position luck and course experience the deciding factor; Watch Tower's Naas winning form at 7f Good and Colin Keane's positional intelligence give him an edge in a chaotic shape, while horses on the outer may find clear runs materialising unexpectedly late.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tower to be ridden close to Little Empire from the outset — if Colin Keane secures the rail and travels second throughout, this race shape is essentially tailored to his profile.

Monitor pre-race for Contrary To Law's early positioning: if Ben Coen elects to chase Little Empire aggressively in the first two furlongs, the shape shifts from Scenario A toward Scenario B with meaningfully stronger pace.

Barbapapa and Spodo Komodo are both front-runners by instinct drawn into a field where they cannot get their position — watch for them to be caught wide and racing in unnatural restraint from the two-furlong pole, a scenario that typically damages their finishing effort.

Blues Emperor's in-running position is worth monitoring around the three-furlong mark — he needs to be last or second-last and have a clear run materialising; if he is stuck behind a wall of horses on the rail, his chance evaporates regardless of pace shape.

Good ground is consistent throughout the card at Naas (all races returning Good) and there is no rail bias or watering variation to factor — the shape call is based purely on pace dynamics without a ground-position skew.

races.name: Naas Racecourse Race

runners_data.name: Fort Vega
runners_data.note: Solid Good-ground performer (3W7P in similar conditions) with a strong recent form string of 125-23 at OR 96, but her natural prominent style means she is competing for a position that Phenomenal Filly is better placed to claim in a four-runner field, pushing Fort Vega further back than ideal; Rory Cleary will need to be creative tactically, and the 38-day absence is not a concern given prior fitness.|

runners_data.name: Dark Willow
runners_data.note: A long 245-day absence is the immediate red flag, and her form figures (80408-) leave little encouragement even when fresh; flagged for finishing fade, she needs a collapse in front to get involved and her hold-up style at least keeps her out of early trouble, but Good ground has yielded only 9 finishes from 13 attempts with no wins or placed runs to show for it.|

runners_data.name: Phenomenal Filly
runners_data.note: P Twomey's yard is in decent form (2/9 over 14 days) and this filly's 7f Good-ground record (2/7f/GOO, 1/7f/GOO among her last four) reads well for this track and conditions; at only 13 days since her last run she arrives fresh and sharp, and wearing headgear (p) for the first time could sharpen her response to Suzie Songs' early move, making her the most natural beneficiary of the race shape.|

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, Colin Keane takes over on a filly with a clean six-from-six record on similar Good ground and a prior course win over 6f; her style-fit tag (0.93) reflects the fact that she is slotted into a role slightly outside her natural profile in this analysis, but in practice she is most likely to lead and set the race's tempo — the key question is whether she can sustain it over 7f against a quality prominent challenger in Phenomenal Filly.|

races.paceDynamic: Suzie Songs is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just four, she should be able to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without being pressured into setting a suicidal pace. Phenomenal Filly and Fort Vega are both prominent-style horses, meaning the field carries more pace than the compact race shape can naturally accommodate — Fort Vega is the more likely of the two to be squeezed back from its natural position, with Phenomenal Filly the better-credentialled prominent runner likely to sit closest to Suzie Songs. Dark Willow is a genuine hold-up horse but her form figures and finish-fade flag make her a peripheral threat at best. With a controlled, uncontested lead on Good ground over 7f, this race shape strongly favours horses that can sit within a length or two of the pace and sustain their effort — the prominent profile, specifically Phenomenal Filly, is best placed to exploit the predictable tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs sets an uncontested, measured gallop and Phenomenal Filly tracks her comfortably.
scenarios.body: Suzie Songs dictates a fair but not punishing pace, and Phenomenal Filly, sitting a length or two off the shoulder, has enough in reserve to pounce inside the final furlong; her Good-ground form (3/4 similar-going runs in the frame) and fresh 13-day return suits this shape perfectly. Fort Vega may chase hard from further back but racing out of its natural prominent role blunts its chance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs sets a genuinely slow early pace and nothing can sustain a challenge from the turn.
scenarios.body: With only four runners and no serious rival willing to close down Suzie Songs, she conserves enough energy to kick again in the final two furlongs and hold every challenger; Colin Keane's high-level tactical awareness and the mare's healthy Good-ground profile (6/6 similar going) give this shape real credibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Collide, Closer Sneaks
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs and Phenomenal Filly burn each other off contesting early position and the race unravels in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A contested early lead lifts the tempo above sustainable, leaving both prominent runners vulnerable late; Fort Vega, though redistributed from its preferred spot, at least has the class (OR 96) and Good-ground form to pick up the pieces if the race falls apart in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the straight and Dark Willow finds late momentum from the back.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires an unusually fast early gallop that burns out all three prominent types simultaneously, an unlikely outcome given the small field and Suzie Songs' tendency to dictate sensibly; Dark Willow's 245-day absence, poor recent form figures, and flagged fade-in-finish make her an unreliable beneficiary even if the shape materialises.

watchPoints.text: Phenomenal Filly is the one to watch tracking Suzie Songs — if W J Lee slots her into a close second position from the off, she has the form and fitness to pounce in the straight and nothing in this field has the late pace to reel her in.

Fort Vega's redistribution from prominent to midfield is a genuine tactical concern — watch whether Rory Cleary pushes forward aggressively at the break to reclaim her natural position, as that decision will reshape the pace picture entirely.

Suzie Songs' stamina for 7f is a question to monitor — she has raced at the trip but her best form includes a 6f win, and if she ties up approaching the final furlong Colin Keane will need to have covered enough ground in front to hold on.

Dark Willow's 245-day absence and fade flag make her effectively a race-fitness watch — if she shows early signs of travelling well for Gavin Ryan it would be a notable positive, but the form profile suggests she is here to complete rather than compete.
